questions.question: What is the general molecular formula for the alkene family of hydrocarbons? (FBISE 2024-II)
questions.explanation: Alkenes (olefins) are unsaturated hydrocarbons possessing one carbon-carbon double bond, conforming to the general formula $C_nH_{2n}$.

questions.question: Which gas is widely used with oxygen in oxy-acetylene torches to produce temperatures up to 3300°C for welding and cutting metals? (FBISE 2023-I, 2025 Model)
questions.explanation: Acetylene ($C_2H_2$) burns in pure oxygen with an intensely hot flame reaching temperatures up to 3300°C, making it indispensable for oxy-acetylene welding and metal cutting.

questions.question: Halogenation of methane in diffused sunlight does NOT produce which of the following compounds? (FBISE 2025 Model)
questions.explanation: In diffused sunlight, methane undergoes stepwise free radical substitution to form $CH_3Cl$, $CH_2Cl_2$, $CHCl_3$, and $CCl_4$. Carbon black is produced by incomplete combustion or direct explosive reaction in bright sunlight, not by diffuse halogenation.

questions.question: The chemical test used to confirm unsaturation (double or triple bonds) in organic molecules by decolorizing reddish-brown color is: (FBISE 2022-II, 2024-I)
questions.explanation: Bromine water ($Br_2$ in water/CCl4) has a reddish-brown color. When shaken with an unsaturated hydrocarbon (alkene or alkyne), bromine adds across the multiple bond, discharging the color.

questions.question: In Baeyer's test, an alkene reacts with cold, dilute alkaline potassium permanganate ($KMnO_4$) solution to produce: (FBISE 2021-II)
questions.explanation: Baeyer's reagent (cold alkaline $KMnO_4$) oxidizes alkenes by hydroxylating both carbons of the double bond, discharging the purple color and yielding a diol (glycol) and brown $MnO_2$ precipitate.

questions.question: Ethene ($C_2H_4$) is industrially prepared by the dehydration of ethanol in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid at: (FBISE 2020-I, 2023-II)
questions.explanation: Heating ethanol ($C_2H_5OH$) with excess concentrated $H_2SO_4$ at 170°C eliminates a molecule of water to produce ethene ($C_2H_4$). At 140°C, diethyl ether is the main product.

questions.question: What is the general molecular formula for the alkyne homologous series? (FBISE 2019-I)
questions.explanation: Alkynes are unsaturated acyclic hydrocarbons with one carbon-carbon triple bond ($-C\equiv C-$) and follow the general formula $C_nH_{2n-2}$.

questions.question: Alkanes are historically known as 'paraffins' because: (FBISE 2018-I, 2022-I)

options.B: They possess little chemical affinity/reactivity (parum affinis)

questions.explanation: The word 'paraffin' is derived from Latin (parum = little, affinis = affinity), reflecting the inert nature of saturated hydrocarbons under standard conditions.

questions.question: Dehydrohalogenation of an alkyl halide involves the removal of: (FBISE 2017-II)
questions.explanation: Dehydrohalogenation is an elimination reaction in which a hydrogen atom and a halogen atom (a hydrogen halide, $HX$) are eliminated from adjacent carbons of an alkyl halide using alcoholic $KOH$.

questions.question: Reduction of an alkyl halide with zinc dust in the presence of dilute aqueous hydrochloric acid yields: (FBISE 2016-II, 2021-I)
questions.explanation: Alkyl halides undergo reduction when treated with $Zn$ and dilute $HCl$, replacing the halogen atom with nascent hydrogen to yield the corresponding alkane: $CH_3Cl + 2[H] \xrightarrow{Zn/HCl} CH_4 + HCl$.

questions.question: Addition of hydrogen (hydrogenation) to ethene in the presence of finely divided nickel catalyst occurs at: (FBISE 2015-I)
questions.explanation: Catalytic hydrogenation of unsaturated hydrocarbons using nickel requires heating to 250°C–300°C. With platinum or palladium catalysts, the reaction can occur at room temperature.

questions.question: Incomplete combustion of methane in a limited supply of oxygen produces: (FBISE 2014-II, 2020-II)

options.B: Carbon monoxide ($CO$), carbon black ($C$), and water ($H_2O$)

questions.explanation: When methane burns in a limited supply of oxygen, incomplete combustion occurs, producing poisonous carbon monoxide ($CO$), finely divided carbon black ($C$), and water: $3CH_4 + 4O_2 \to 2CO + C + 6H_2O$.

questions.question: What is the physical state of the first four members of the alkane series ($C_1$ to $C_4$) at room temperature? (FBISE 2013-I)
questions.explanation: Methane, ethane, propane, and butane are non-polar gases at standard temperature and pressure due to their weak London dispersion forces.

questions.question: Which alkyne is commonly known as acetylene? (FBISE 2019-II)
questions.explanation: Ethyne ($C_2H_2$, $H-C\equiv C-H$) is universally known by its common name acetylene, the simplest and most industrially significant alkyne.

questions.question: Vicinal dihalides are organic compounds that contain: (FBISE 2018-II)

options.A: Two halogen atoms attached to the same carbon atom
options.B: Two halogen atoms attached to adjacent carbon atoms
options.C: Halogen atoms at the two terminal ends of a long chain
options.D: Four halogen atoms attached to one carbon

questions.explanation: Vicinal (from Latin vicinus = neighbor) dihalides have halogen atoms bonded to adjacent carbon atoms (e.g., 1,2-dibromoethane: $CH_2Br-CH_2Br$).

questions.question: When ethyne is treated with cold alkaline $KMnO_4$, the final oxidation product formed is: (FBISE 2017-I)
questions.explanation: Alkaline $KMnO_4$ oxidizes the triple bond of ethyne completely through intermediate glyoxal ($CHO-CHO$) to produce dicarboxylic oxalic acid ($HOOC-COOH$).

questions.question: Which of the following hydrocarbons burns with a luminous, sooty (smoky) flame due to its high carbon-to-hydrogen ratio?
questions.explanation: Acetylene has a 1:1 carbon-to-hydrogen atomic ratio (92.3% carbon by mass). In air, unburnt carbon particles become incandescenly hot, causing a bright, smoky, sooty flame.

questions.question: What is the IUPAC name for $CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_3$?
questions.explanation: The longest continuous carbon chain consists of three carbon atoms (propane), with a methyl substituent at carbon-2, giving the IUPAC name 2-methylpropane (isobutane is its common name).

questions.question: What is the product formed when 1,2-dibromoethane is heated with zinc dust?
questions.explanation: Dehalogenation of a vicinal dihalide with zinc dust removes both halogen atoms to form a double bond: $CH_2Br-CH_2Br + Zn \to CH_2=CH_2 + ZnBr_2$.

questions.question: Which hydrocarbon is used for the artificial ripening of green agricultural fruits like bananas and mangoes?
questions.explanation: Ethene ($C_2H_4$) is a natural plant hormone that triggers fruit ripening, and is used commercially to artificially ripen green fruit under controlled conditions.

questions.question: What is the molecular formula of cyclohexane?
questions.explanation: Cycloalkanes have a ring structure where two hydrogen atoms are lost to close the ring, conforming to the formula $C_nH_{2n}$. Cyclohexane is $C_6H_{12}$.

questions.question: When ethene gas reacts with bromine dissolved in an inert solvent like $CCl_4$, what product is synthesized?
questions.explanation: Bromine electrophilically adds across the double bond of ethene: $CH_2=CH_2 + Br_2 \to CH_2Br-CH_2Br$ (1,2-dibromoethane), discharging the reddish-brown color.

questions.question: Chloroform has which of the following chemical formulas?
questions.explanation: Trichloromethane is commonly known as chloroform ($CHCl_3$). It was historically used as a general anesthetic.

questions.question: Which chemical is utilized as a solvent for fats, oils, and greases, and was formerly used in dry cleaning and fire extinguishers?
questions.explanation: Carbon tetrachloride ($CCl_4$, tetrachloromethane) is a heavy non-flammable liquid widely used as an industrial solvent and historically in fire extinguishers under the trade name Pyrene.

questions.question: What happens when methane is exposed to chlorine in direct, bright sunlight?

options.B: An explosive reaction occurs yielding carbon black and $HCl$

questions.explanation: In direct, bright sunlight, the reaction between methane and chlorine is instantaneous and explosive: $CH_4 + 2Cl_2 \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} C(s) + 4HCl(g)$, depositing carbon black.

questions.question: What is the hybridization of carbon atoms in an ethyne ($H-C\equiv C-H$) molecule?
questions.explanation: In ethyne, each carbon atom forms one $\sigma$ bond to hydrogen and one $\sigma$ bond to the other carbon, utilizing two $sp$ hybrid orbitals arranged in a linear geometry (180°).

questions.question: How many sigma ($\sigma$) and pi ($\pi$) bonds are present in an ethyne ($C_2H_2$) molecule?
questions.explanation: In $H-C\equiv C-H$, each $C-H$ bond is a $\sigma$ bond (2 $\sigma$) and the triple bond consists of one $\sigma$ bond and two $\pi$ bonds. Total = 3 $\sigma$ and 2 $\pi$ bonds.

questions.question: What is the shape and bond angle of a methane ($CH_4$) molecule?
questions.explanation: Carbon in methane undergoes $sp^3$ hybridization, directing four equivalent bonding orbitals toward the corners of a regular tetrahedron with $H-C-H$ bond angles of 109.5°.

questions.question: Which of the following reagents is used to dehydrate ethanol to ethene?
questions.explanation: Concentrated sulphuric acid is an exceptional dehydrating agent. At 170°C, it extracts a molecule of water from ethanol ($C_2H_5OH$) to yield ethene.

questions.question: What type of chemical reaction is characteristic of alkanes?
questions.explanation: Because alkanes are saturated with strong $C-C$ and $C-H$ single $\sigma$ bonds, they do not undergo addition reactions. Instead, they react via free radical substitution (e.g., photochemical halogenation).

questions.question: What type of chemical reaction is characteristic of alkenes and alkynes?
questions.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons possess relatively weak and exposed $\pi$ electron clouds that readily open up to add atoms or groups across the multiple bond without loss of carbon atoms.

questions.question: What catalyst and temperature are used to convert vegetable oil into vegetable ghee (solid fat)?
questions.explanation: Industrial hydrogenation of polyunsaturated vegetable oils to produce solid vegetable ghee uses finely divided nickel ($Ni$) catalyst at approximately 250°C under moderate hydrogen pressure.

questions.question: When propane undergoes complete combustion in oxygen, what is the stoichiometric coefficient of $O_2$ in the balanced equation: $C_3H_8 + xO_2 \to 3CO_2 + 4H_2O$?
questions.explanation: Balancing oxygen atoms: $3 \times 2 (\text{in } CO_2) + 4 \times 1 (\text{in } H_2O) = 10$ oxygen atoms. Therefore, $10 / 2 = 5$ moles of $O_2$ are required.

questions.question: Which of the following hydrocarbons has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: In a homologous series of unbranched alkanes, as the molecular mass and chain length increase, the surface area increases, strengthening London dispersion forces and raising boiling points.

questions.question: What gas is generated when calcium carbide ($CaC_2$) reacts with water?
questions.explanation: Reaction of calcium carbide with water is a traditional laboratory and industrial method to generate acetylene: $CaC_2 + 2H_2O \to C_2H_2\uparrow + Ca(OH)_2$.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: $C_3H_6$ conforms to the formula $C_nH_{2n}$ (propene) and contains a carbon-carbon double bond, classifying it as an unsaturated hydrocarbon.

questions.question: What is the molecular formula of the alkyne containing 5 carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Using the alkyne formula $C_nH_{2n-2}$ with $n = 5$: $C_5H_{2(5)-2} = C_5H_8$ (pentyne).

questions.question: Marsh gas is a common historical name for which hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Methane is produced by the anaerobic bacterial decomposition of plant matter in swamps and marshes, hence its historical name 'marsh gas'.

questions.question: The conversion of ethene to polyethene (polythene) is an example of:
questions.explanation: Ethene molecules link together by breaking their double bonds under high pressure and temperature with a catalyst, forming the long-chain polymer polythene via addition polymerization.

questions.question: Which of the following reagents can be used to distinguish between ethane (an alkane) and ethene (an alkene)?
questions.explanation: Ethene quickly decolorizes both reddish-brown bromine water and purple alkaline $KMnO_4$ (Baeyer's test) due to addition across its double bond, whereas saturated ethane does not react under standard conditions.
